usage: Official primary-source architectural references. These sources do not certify or validate this project. Paraphrases are intentionally short; architecture choices are design inferences.

sources.title: Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS)
sources.locator: Overview; Water Recovery System; Air Revitalization System; Oxygen Generation System
sources.verified_paraphrase: ECLSS manages atmospheric pressure, oxygen, ventilation, fire protection, water, and waste. Water recovery, air revitalization, and oxygen generation are distinct interacting subsystems.
sources.design_inference: Separate habitat service domains, each with qualified local control, health reporting, maintenance, and traceable sensor quality. A single environmental sensor or display cannot substitute for these systems.
sources.limits: ISS hardware descriptions do not establish our habitat's sizing, atmospheric setpoints, redundancy, or crew suitability.

sources.title: State-of-the-Art of Small Spacecraft Technology — 3.0 Power
sources.locator: 3.1 Introduction; 3.6 State-of-the-Art — Power Management and Distribution
sources.verified_paraphrase: Spacecraft power systems include generation, storage, and distribution. PMAD regulates and distributes electricity, incorporates fault management, and interfaces with onboard computers for monitoring.
sources.design_inference: Represent these functions separately in the asset and telemetry model; retain electrical protection and qualified load actions in local equipment.
sources.limits: This is a small-spacecraft reference; catalog voltages, products, and capacities are not habitat design values.

sources.title: Integrated System for Autonomous and Adaptive Caretaking (ISAAC)
sources.verified_paraphrase: ISAAC investigated autonomous spacecraft caretaking during uncrewed phases, combining robotic inspection and subsystem telemetry, inventory work, and coordinated cargo handling.
sources.design_inference: RockstarOS should unify equipment health, inspection evidence, inventory, and work execution locally, rather than depend on uninterrupted remote supervision.
sources.limits: ISAAC demonstrations are not evidence that this project's autonomy or physical equipment works.

sources.title: NASA-STD-8739.8B — Software Assurance and Software Safety Standard
sources.verified_paraphrase: Software hazard analysis considers common-mode failures in redundant computers and should preserve the independence of hazard inhibits and hardware redundancy.
sources.design_inference: Independent local protection must not share all of its failure causes with Core, UI, AI, or their network. Two computers running identical software alone do not demonstrate independence.
sources.limits: Using this principle is not NASA standards compliance or human-rating; project-specific hazard analysis remains required.

sources.title: SWE-134 — Safety-Critical Software Design Requirements, Handbook Version D
sources.verified_paraphrase: The requirements address known safe initialization and transitions, command order and prerequisites, input/output integrity, fault handling, and responses within hazard-prevention deadlines.
sources.design_inference: Define equipment-specific restart and fault states; validate command preconditions at the equipment boundary. Do not define a universal safe state as all power off.
sources.limits: Our implementation has no completed safety or mission-critical qualification. Hazard-specific deadlines and acceptable states need physical-system analysis.

sources.title: RFC 9171 — Bundle Protocol Version 7
sources.locator: 4.3.1 Primary Bundle Block, Lifetime; 5.1 Generation of Administrative Records; 6.1.1 Bundle Status Reports
sources.verified_paraphrase: BPv7 supports store-and-forward communication with bundle lifetime processing. Status reports describe bundle progress, and their generation is disabled by default to limit excessive traffic.
sources.design_inference: Treat transfer status separately from application acceptance and equipment completion. Add application authorization, expiry, deduplication, state checks, and result reconciliation.
sources.limits: The simulator does not implement BPv7. Existing A-LINK software must not be described as a BPv7-compatible system without profile and interoperability tests.

sources.title: RFC 9172 — Bundle Protocol Security
sources.locator: 3.1 Block Definitions; Security Context and Security Policy sections
sources.verified_paraphrase: BPSec defines integrity and confidentiality security blocks and relies on security policy and security contexts for their application.
sources.design_inference: A future BPv7 profile must specify keys, policies, and contexts; transport cryptography does not replace local command authority or equipment preconditions.
sources.limits: This is an architectural candidate, not an implemented BPSec feature or established key infrastructure.

sources.title: CCSDS 133.0-B-2 — Space Packet Protocol, Issue 2 with Editorial Change 2
sources.locator: Scope; Protocol Overview; Protocol Data Unit
sources.verified_paraphrase: Space Packet Protocol specifies services and packet procedures for transferring application data with CCSDS packet structures.
sources.design_inference: Use an explicitly selected spacecraft packet profile at a mission gateway while preserving separate application semantics, authority, and command-result tracking.
sources.limits: Packet encoding alone does not provide full mission interoperability, end-to-end delivery, equipment authorization, or BPv7 functionality.

sources.title: Gateway Deep Space Logistics
sources.verified_paraphrase: NASA describes deep-space logistics as transportation of cargo, equipment and consumables.
sources.design_inference: Separate launch injection, cargo transfer, receiving, and equipment commissioning in the project.
sources.limits: This does not establish available cargo capacity, a vehicle selection, or a mission schedule for this project.
